title: Fixing the paper's citations and claims
answer:
**Bottom line.** The paper's positioning was wrong in three ways that this run's own controls already settle, and the measurement companion was positioned against the wrong literature. This artifact strikes two load-bearing qualifiers, narrows a third, gives the measurement result 21 neighbours it never had, quotes the named consumers instead of paraphrasing them, and repairs five citations. Every quote below was extracted by regex from the primary PDF or HTML and re-checked by `scripts/self_check.py` (36 rows, 34 VERIFIED-QUOTE, 2 CARRIED, longest quote 39 words, all passing); every number about this run carries the workspace-relative path of the file that produced it, and all 33 such paths were opened this session and resolve (`results/path_lint.md`). No API calls were made; OpenRouter spend $0.00.

**(1) Three qualifiers struck, one narrowed.** (a) "The effective region differs between two sibling checkpoints" is FALSIFIED by this run's own evidence: the development-named band lost at matched energy at both levels (E2 0.50 vs 0.59, E3 0.30 vs 0.53, recorded NAMED_AND_LOST), the sibling's causal profile predicts the anchor's 50 weight cells at rho -0.442 — no worse than it predicts its own panel at -0.278 and -0.111 — and the two production kernels are statistically indistinguishable once dose is matched (-0.029 [-0.129, +0.071], p 0.774; 0.000 [-0.086, +0.086], p 1.000) (`round-4/experiment-14/src/results/report_tables.md`, Tables 4, 6, 6b, 7). (b) "It decides it differently per language" is falsified for the BAND: the language-label placebo does not collapse, with the English causal write profile predicting the Slovene residual at rho -0.94 (`round-4/experiment-13/src/results/analysis.json`, `language_swapped_O_spearman` -0.941). What does differ by language is the residual left at the same placement and energy (strict refusal 0.07 EN vs 0.27 SL). (c) "Selection blindness explains the divergent search outcomes" is unavailable: the frozen primary prediction was falsified (+0.006 [0.000, 0.019], CI includes zero; judge-referenced the sign reverses to -0.029 [-0.060, -0.005]) (`round-4/experiment-15/src/results/analysis.json`). (d) The surviving matched-budget qualifier is NARROWED, not kept whole — see (2).

**The kept delta, one sentence.** At matched total removal energy AND matched layer count, where in depth a Heretic-family English-derived weight edit deposits its removal energy orders how much refusal survives — in English and in Slovene, in two sibling checkpoints and in an outside family — while doubling the dose of the badly placed edit does not buy what the well-placed edit buys at half the energy. It is an ordering result on matched contrasts, not a band prescription.

**(2) The positive's largest narrowing is a paper the draft never cited.** Li et al. (ICLR 2025) already report "a small set of contiguous layers in the middle of the model that are crucial for distinguishing malicious queries from normal ones", and — decisively for this run — already compare layer RANGES in weight space, evaluating "the impact of different layer ranges on the security of aligned LLMs by scaling the parameter weights of the layers within the range", refining the bounds with an over-rejection count [21]. So "a contiguous mid-depth band is safety-critical" and "compare depth ranges by editing their weights" are both prior work. What survives is narrower: the contrast at matched total energy AND matched layer count, a removal rather than an amplification edit, two languages, and an outside-family replication. A second neighbour sets a different boundary: Hadetskyi et al. find that uniformly spread layer selection "substantially outperform[s] norm-based selection (targeting layers with the highest refusal signal norm)" by up to ~70pp [22]. That is a comparison of SELECTION CRITERIA, not of placements at matched budget, so it does not conflict with this run — the reconciliation sentence is in `results/depth_attribution_provenance.md`. The adversarial searches for a prior dose-versus-placement exchange result returned nothing closer than an iso-effect dose-response study of steering under quantisation [23] and a discriminative layer-selection rule for steering [24]; the absence is therefore stated as "not found by these queries" with rows 37, 38, 39 and 43 logged.

**(3) The measurement result's real neighbours, three of which shrink it.** The draft cited AdvPrefix against the depth finding; that is the wrong target. AdvPrefix owns objective misspecification inside an optimiser — "Misspecified: even with low optimization loss, actual responses are often incomplete or unfaithful" [7] — and belongs to the selection-blindness companion, where this run's contribution is the weight-edit instance (structural threshold blindness in BOTH searches, threshold-blind fraction 1.00, plus a calibration difference of slope 0.31 vs 0.74 and floor 72 vs 16). On the substring-metric side, StrongREJECT already owns the evaluation-time point: "Most of the baseline automated evaluators overestimate how effective jailbreak methods are on average, especially string matching for non-refusal" [1]. More damagingly for the draft's framing, the abliteration-specific version is already published: across 20 original-and-abliterated systems, "regex tends to overestimate refusals by flagging templated disclaimers in otherwise harmless answers" [3], and a Heretic-including tool comparison states the same caveat, that marker matching "can produce false positives (responses that mention safety language while still providing actionable content)" [4]. A community abliteration tool independently documents a model claiming 3/100 refusals measuring 60/100 under a stricter pipeline [19], and an open benchmark defect report records refusal prefixes "matched anywhere rather than as a prefix" [20]. Two further pieces of context bound how much of this is new: the attack literature optimises directly against refusal substrings rather than auditing them [5], and metric quality for harmfulness is itself contested, with reference-based metrics sometimes beating LLM judges [6]. One expectation in this artifact's own plan did not survive contact with the source: a recent evaluator measurement study was named as the closest neighbour here, but full-text inspection shows it compares six LLM-based evaluators and treats string matching only as background, "fully reproducible, but it provides only a weak proxy for actual compliance" [2]. What survives for this run is the magnitude and direction on its own checkpoints (keyword .851 vs judged .255 on the shipped Gemma English edit, false-positive share .761, kappa -.04, `round-2/experiment-4/src/README.md` §4), the WITHIN-edited agreement on held-out harm categories (keyword kappa 0.02 EN / 0.00 SL against a distilled classifier at 0.48 / 0.73, `round-4/experiment-15/src/results/analysis.json`), and that this same counter was the optimiser's objective.

**(4) The judge and guard story, with the contradicting evidence stated.** That a scorer certified on one output distribution degrades on a shifted one is published and audited: judges validated on static held-out sets "degrade to near random chance" under red-teaming shift, over 6,642 human-verified labels [8]. That judge reliability is "language-conditional rather than uniform" is likewise established, in a survey of 33 multilingual LLM-as-judge papers [15], and judge-human agreement is reported to drop "in lower-resource languages and less commonly supported scripts" in a jailbreak benchmark [16]. Judges are also known to hold their priors against a changed safety definition [18] and to be flippable by benign framing wrappers [34], both of which describe the surface form that caveat-laden edited outputs take. So this run's Slovene judge-gate failures (within-edited SL 0.723-0.744 against EN 0.856-0.871) INSTANTIATE a known problem rather than discover one. Crucially, there is contradicting evidence against the strong reading: a frontier judge validated per language on 300 stratified responses across ten languages reaches "κ = 0.80–0.83, with 93.2–96.6% binary" agreement, and 22 of 61 model configurations there are more vulnerable in English than in low-resource languages [17]. The paper must therefore claim only that ITS English-certified local judge lost agreement in Slovene inside the edited condition. On the guard side, reporting a guard and a judge separately for abliterated checkpoints is already practice — and the published result is agreement, not divergence: "Overall, the two methods are in strong agreement, with differences of at most 4 percentage points" [9]. This run's finding is the opposite and is language-dependent (official-guard ASR .738 EN vs .103 SL on the shipped Gemma edit; Slovene non-refusals guard-safe more often by +0.232 [0.124, 0.348], `round-4/evaluation-2/src/results/asr_summary.json`), and no neighbour running that comparison was found by these queries (rows 32, 33, 47). Three further pieces fix the vocabulary: the three-way moderation framing of prompt harm, response harm and refusal [10], XSTest's "Partial Refusal is any combination of refusal and compliance" [11] and a pragmatics taxonomy of refusal forms [12]; and the conceptual anticipation of this run's actionability reading is explicit — "What fails to transfer is calibration of the safety decision, not the underlying representation" [14].

**(5) The consumers, quoted rather than straw-manned, with the claim softened accordingly.** Yoon, Park and Ritter state plainly that "In our main experiment, we instantiate Munalg using a safety-ablated (abliterated) version of the models", including a gemma-3-27b-it checkpoint, and define the quantity as a helpfulness win rate "as the win rate of Munalg against Malign on helpfulness judgments" on benign prompts [25]. Their language-neutrality argument rests on direction universality — safety ablation acts on a shared axis "and thus does not inherently introduce language-specific biases" [25] — which is exactly the assumption this run's per-language residual bears on. But the bias sentence must be softened, because they do check a version of the confound: an Alignment Gap Difference axis on P-MMEval, with points near zero taken to show that "Safety Cost is a distinct phenomenon, not just a side" effect of ablation, plus a from-scratch matched-checkpoint replication in §4.4 [25]. The honest claim is that this run's evidence bears on a channel their check does not cover — residual refusal per language inside the counterfactual — not that their estimate is wrong. RefusEU is the second instance of the same practice ("To collect unsafe answers, we use an abliterated" Llama-3.1-70B lorablated variant) and, usefully for the write-up, its guard pipeline is a specific pair (Llama-Guard-3-8B and PolyGuard-Qwen), which the paper should name instead of writing "the official guard" [13].

**(6) The origin credits, and a mis-citation.** The English-proxy-under-reports-non-English-damage principle is prior work and is credited, not claimed: quantisation damage under-reported by automatic metrics [26], activation-decided weight importance in Wanda, which prunes "with the smallest magnitudes multiplied by the corresponding input activations" [29], and in AWQ, which insists one should "refer to the activation distribution, not weights" [30], and calibration-language effects for quantised multilingual models, where "non-English and multilingual calibration sets significantly improve perplexity compared to English-only baselines" [28]. This run's own realized-exposure operationalisation of that principle was tested and FAILED (dR² -0.011 [-0.058, 0.027], `round-2/experiment-6/src/results/analysis_results.json`) and belongs in the falsified column. One citation is wrong in direction: the pruning-calibration reference's published title is *On the Limitations of Language-targeted Pruning* (TACL vol. 14, pp. 167-192, anthology 2026.tacl-1.9 [31]), and its finding is that "while calibration on the target language effectively retains perplexity and yields high signal-to-noise ratios, it does not consistently improve downstream task performance" [27]. It cannot be cited as support for "the calibration language matters" in the strong sense the run's motivation uses.

**(7) The four bibliography defects, resolved.** [19] in the draft is Li, Yao, Zhang and Li, *Safety Layers in Aligned Large Language Models: The Key to LLM Security*, **ICLR 2025**, **arXiv:2408.17003** — the draft says ICLR 2024 and gives no id; note also that the v1 title reads "Safety Layers OF Aligned…", so the published "IN" form should be cited [21]. [20] is Bosco and Srinivasan, *Locating and Steering Refusal Beyond Attention*, **arXiv:2609.04721**, a preprint with no venue [33]. [21] is Jiang, *Refit the Probe: Single-Direction Ablation Is Not a Necessity Test*, **arXiv:2606.00926** (v2), also a preprint [32]. The fourth defect is the AdvPrefix placement, corrected in (3). BibTeX-ready field sets are in `results/bibliography_repairs.md`.

**(8) The depth-attribution provenance, stated exactly.** The "2–3 middle layers" sentence DOES exist in arXiv 2607.02714 §3.2 as that paper's own attribution to Arditi et al.; the attribution was not found in Arditi et al. (2406.11717v3) by the dependency's queries; and 2607.02714 rejects it in the next sentence, opting for uniformly spread selection instead [22]. The NOT VERIFIED flag attaches to the ATTRIBUTION only — not to the sentence's existence in 2607.02714, and not to the uniform-spread finding, which is verified with its locator. It must never be cited as a standing depth fact. The properly attributable home for "a contiguous mid-depth band is safety-critical" is arXiv 2408.17003 [21].

**Confidence.** High for the citation repairs, the quote verification and the three struck qualifiers: each rests on a primary-source extract saved in `results/raw/` or on a result file in this run whose path was opened this session. Moderate for the absence claims, which are evidenced by 22 logged queries rather than proven, and which a US-region English-only search engine could miss; each names what would falsify it. Moderate for the completeness of the narrowing: two of the six neighbours the plan predicted would shrink the delta shrank it more than expected (2408.17003, 2510.02768), one behaved oppositely to the plan's description (2505.19056 reports agreement, not divergence), one contradicts the strong form of a claim (2605.17173), and two of the plan's own factual expectations about sources proved wrong on full-text inspection (2609.10594, 2607.02235) — which is evidence that unchecked plan assumptions in this area do not survive contact with the PDFs, and a reason to expect further narrowing if more queries are run. What would change the conclusions: any paper that moves a fixed number of edited layers to a different depth at fixed total edit magnitude (kills A1), or reports a refusal proxy's agreement separately for unedited and edited conditions in more than one language (kills A4), or reports guard and judge rates per language on one edited checkpoint (kills A5).
